paper_summary: Orbulov and Majlinger characterise the microstructure of SL150 and SL300 ceramic hollow microspheres (Envirospheres Ltd.) and of the aluminium matrix syntactic foams (MMSFs) made from them by pressure infiltration with Al99.5, AlSi12, AlMgSi1 and AlCu5 matrices at ~60 vol% microspheres. SEM plus map and line EDS show the microsphere wall is built from Al2O3 needles (5-10 um long, <0.5 um diameter) embedded in a mullite + amorphous SiO2 matrix, and that molten aluminium reduces the SiO2-rich zones (4Al + 3SiO2 -> 2Al2O3 + 3Si), degrading the sphere wall and forming gamma-Al2O3. The reaction was intensive with Al99.5, AlMgSi1 and AlCu5 matrices but suppressed with AlSi12 (high matrix Si lowers the driving force) and for Al99.5-SL300 infiltrated at the lower temperature of 690 C; interface layers were ~2-4 um (AlMgSi1), ~3 um (AlCu5) and <1.5 um (AlSi12), with Mg dissolving into the wall for AlMgSi1 and CuAl2 precipitating on it for AlCu5. The paper reports no mechanical property measurements.

processing.particle_grade: SL150 (Envirospheres Ltd., Australia; 30-35 wt% Al2O3, 45-50 wt% amorphous SiO2, 19 wt% mullite, 1 wt% quartz)

structure.microstructure_notes: Particle (microballoon) porosity 50.9%, total porosity 44.7%. Microsphere size range 56-183 um, specific surface 0.060 um^-1. Microsphere wall = Al2O3 needles (5-10 um long, <0.5 um diameter) embedded in a mixture of mullite and amorphous SiO2. XRD phase constitution of the foam (Table 3, measured in this paper): Al 67, Si 8, mullite 11, alpha-Al2O3 3, gamma-Al2O3 11, amorphous 0 wt%. Reductive reaction 4Al(liq)+3SiO2(sol)->2Al2O3(sol)+3Si(sol) was intensive: 11 wt% gamma-Al2O3 formed and no amorphous phase remained; the microsphere walls were severely degraded (Fig. 4a).

test.specimen_notes: No mechanical test in this paper. Characterisation only: density/porosity (Table 2, taken from ref. [3]), XRD phase analysis (Phillips X-Pert, CuKa lambda=0.154186 nm, 40 kV / 35 mA, goniometer 0.04 deg/s), SEM (Phillips XL-30) and map/line EDS (EDAX Genesis; 15 kV for maps on bare microspheres, 20 kV for line scans on polished foam cross sections, 100 points per line, 20 s per point).

extraction_notes:
IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this is a purely microstructural/analytical paper (SEM, map and line EDS, XRD). It contains NO mechanical, thermal or physical property measurements of the foams, so every field in Properties is null in all eight records. The records capture the processing and structure data (matrix, microsphere grade and size, volume fraction, densities, porosities, XRD phase constitution, matrix-particle reaction state) for the eight matrix x microsphere combinations.

data_origin: the density and porosity values in Table 2 are explicitly cited to reference [3] (I. N. Orbulov, J. Dobranszky, Periodica Polytechnica Mechanical Engineering, 52(2008)35-42), the same authors' earlier paper, so all eight records are marked 'secondary' with that citation in sample_label. The XRD phase constitutions of Table 3 and all EDS/SEM observations were measured in this paper (primary) and are recorded in microstructure_notes rather than as separate records.

Unit conversions: porosity percentages converted to fractions for matrix_porosity_fraction (e.g. -6.2% -> -0.062). Matrix porosity is negative for the Al99.5, AlMgSi1 and AlCu5 foams because the measured density exceeded the theoretical one, which the authors attribute to microspheres that were themselves infiltrated. Note an internal inconsistency: the text says 'the values of matrix porosity are always remained below 8%' while Table 2 lists -13.4% (AlMgSi1-SL150) and -12.2% (AlCu5-SL300); Table 2 values were used as printed. Table 2 here also differs slightly from the same data in the authors' companion paper (W136470296): matrix porosity -6.2 vs -6.3% for Al99.5-SL150, and theoretical density 1.42 vs 1.41 g/cm3 for Al99.5-SL300.

particle_volume_fraction = 0.60 comes from the text ('The volume fraction of the microspheres was maintained at relatively high (~60 vol%) level'); it is a nominal target, not a per-block measurement. The 50.9% / 48.2% values in Table 2 are the porosity contributed by the hollow interiors, not the sphere volume fraction, and are kept in microstructure_notes. particle_true_density_g_cc and particle_wall_thickness_ratio are null because Table 1 of this paper gives average diameter, size range and specific surface but no wall thickness or density. cure_or_process_temperature_c is filled only for Al99.5-SL300 (690 C, the only infiltration temperature stated numerically); the others are described only as higher. test_type is 'other' (density / XRD / SEM-EDS characterisation, no mechanical loading) and test temperature is left null since none is stated. Quartz content is given as 1 wt% and mullite 19 wt% in Table 1 of this paper (the companion paper quotes 15-20% mullite and 0-5% quartz ranges). Literature results cited in the introduction were not turned into records.
